Sydney Opera House, Sydney, New South Wales, Australia
The Sydney Opera House is one of the world’s most iconic buildings and represents a unique combination of architecture, culture, and exhibition art. After initial ideas for a large opera and concert hall in Sydney were put forward in 1947, Danish architect Jørn Utzon won the international competition in 1956 with an avant-garde design whose striking sail-like shell structure accentuates Bennelong Bay. Construction was significantly delayed, causing cost overruns and political disputes. From 1959 to 1973, under a succession of planners and engineers, shell-shaped roof structures were built, which later served as railing systems and spectator areas.
The opening in 1973 by Queen Elizabeth II marked the beginning of a global success story as a music, opera, and festival venue. In 2007, the ensemble became a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is considered a masterpiece of modern architecture, and dominates Sydney’s skyline as a symbol of cultural innovation and creative power.

ImageDescription.value:
Sydney Opera House, Sydney, New South Wales, Australia
The Sydney Opera House is one of the world’s most iconic buildings and represents a unique combination of architecture, culture, and exhibition art. After initial ideas for a large opera and concert hall in Sydney were put forward in 1947, Danish architect Jørn Utzon won the international competition in 1956 with an avant-garde design whose striking sail-like shell structure accentuates Bennelong Bay. Construction was significantly delayed, causing cost overruns and political disputes. From 1959 to 1973, under a succession of planners and engineers, shell-shaped roof structures were built, which later served as railing systems and spectator areas.
The opening in 1973 by Queen Elizabeth II marked the beginning of a global success story as a music, opera, and festival venue. In 2007, the ensemble became a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is considered a masterpiece of modern architecture, and dominates Sydney’s skyline as a symbol of cultural innovation and creative power.

ImageDescription.value: Sydney Opera House at night. I took this image during the 2016 Sydney Vivid Festival. I stood in the middle of the Sydney Harbour Bridge for this 32 second exposure. The vantage point was excellent but it’s also the shakiest part of the bridge for this long exposure, every time a large truck or a train went past it ruined the shot with vibrations. It took around 20 attempts until I finally had a 32 second window that was relatively free of vibrations. The camera battery died straight after I captured this image. I am deeply honoured to be the first Australian to become a finalist in the - Wiki Loves Monuments Picture of the Year 2017 with this photo. Feel free to download it - it belongs to the world now.
